items.title: Live: Next round of US-Iran talks could be within a week
items.description: The next round of talks between the US and Iran could take place this week or early next week, an Iranian embassy official in Pakistan tells Reuters. Follow live.

items.title: Breaking: Magnitude-4.5 earthquake felt across large parts of NSW
items.description: The NSW Central West has been hit by a one of the largest earthquakes ever recorded in the region.

items.title: Billionaire's 'slow moving car crash' leads to individuals being investigated by ASIC
items.description: After years of financial red flags, corporate watchdog ASIC confirms it has multiple investigations underway into Sanjeev Gupta's troubled empire, following multiple collapses that have left hundreds of workers facing an uncertain future.

items.title: The warning signs a health practitioner wants to exploit your superannuation
items.description: The healthcare regulator and tax office are cracking down on health practitioners who help patients access their superannuation early after one Perth doctor signed off on a $20,000 withdrawal for liposuction.

items.title: Qantas cuts domestic flights and raises fares as fuel costs blow out
items.description: Qantas will cut domestic flights due to higher fuel costs and the uncertainty of the Middle East war, as it flags as much as $800 million in extra fuel costs.

items.title: Judgement day looming for high-stakes battle of iron ore dynasties
items.description: Gina Rinehart, the wealthiest person in Australia, expects a judgement to be handed down on Wednesday in an explosive court battle with the family of her father's former business partner over iron ore royalties.

items.title: Butters found guilty of abusing umpire as Port claims 'glaring hole in the evidence'
items.description: Port Adelaide star Zak Butters is found guilty of umpire abuse at the AFL Tribunal, despite strongly denying allegations he asked umpire Nick Foot "how much are they paying you?".

items.title: Collard handed monster ban over 'entirely unacceptable' homophobic slur
items.description: St Kilda forward Lance Collard is suspended after a marathon AFL Tribunal hearing with a deliberation of over 90 minutes.

items.title: Prince Harry and Meghan kick off Australia visit with stop at Melbourne hospital
items.description: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have begun their multi-day visit to Australia in Melbourne, meeting with patients at a children's hospital.

items.title: Coalition's migration proposal faces practical questions
items.description: The Coalition's new migration policy aims to increase screening of visa applicants and "boot out" people who do not abide by Australia's values, but questions remain about how the plan would work in practice.

items.title: Fuel excise cut 'too focused on politics', analysts say as concerns grow
items.description: Some energy analysts are questioning the federal government's temporary tax cuts on fuel, warning that lower prices may work against Australia's long-term needs and goals.

items.title: Palestinian groups take Australia to court over Israel arms exports
items.description: A group of Palestinian human rights organisations launch legal action against the defence minister seeking transparency over Australia's arms exports to Israel.

items.title: Harvey Weinstein to face retrial on New York rape charge
items.description: Former Hollywood magnate Harvey Weinstein is again going on trial on a rape charge in New York City. He will remain imprisoned for other offences regardless of the verdict.

items.title: INXS is out, Phil Collins in as Rock & Roll Hall of Fame 2026 inductees announced
items.description: INXS has missed out on landing a place in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame with 2026 inductees including Phil Collins, Queen Latifah and Fela Kuti.

items.title: Kitty Flanagan and Anne Edmonds create comedy chaos in new show
items.description: Plus Nicole Kidman is an Aussie wrestler in Margo's Got Money Troubles, Baby Reindeer's Richard Gadd returns, and the reboots keep on coming with Malcolm in the Middle.

items.title: How I've learnt to embrace the new normal of only having one breast
items.description: I decided to keep my healthy breast, opting against reconstruction. It means I'm now what's known in the community as a uniboober.

items.title: Dash cam video of near-misses on WA highways prompts road safety call
items.description: A 21-year-old woman was charged with reckless driving after dash cam video allegedly caught her overtaking a triple road train in an "unsafe" manner.

items.title: WA children to get needle-free flu vaccine
items.description: Western Australia is offering free needle-free flu vaccines for children in a bid to curb declining inoculation rates and prevent another deadly influenza season.

items.title: Teacher concedes he was 'angry' before 'accidentally' striking student
items.description: A former Darwin teacher who allegedly struck a female student in the face has taken the stand in the Northern Territory Supreme Court, conceding he was "angry" after she swore at him.

items.title: 'Fierce and defiant' disability advocate remembered after drowning
items.description: Ellen Fraser-Barbour is being remembered for her tireless advocacy and love of nature after her death at the age of 35.

items.title: Inquiry told school to lose students if $1.5-billion waste incinerator built
items.description: A school in the middle of a $22-million master plan for its growing enrolment numbers is worried the buildings will not be needed if a waste to energy plant is approved in the town.

items.title: Killers chauffeured interstate after Gavin Preston underworld hit, prosecutors allege
items.description: Prosecutors allege two men were chauffeured back to NSW after conducting a contract killing of the Melbourne underworld figure in 2023.

items.title: Australia's largest cattle feedlot on the market as grain-fed beef surges
items.description: Mort & Co, which fattens hundreds of thousands of cattle on grain before being slaughtered for beef, puts the majority of its assets on the market.

items.title: Blow to cartography in Australia as The Map Shop prepares to close
items.description: One of Australia's few remaining cartography shops is about to close in Adelaide, prompting questions about where people can buy the critical documents, particularly those travelling in remote areas where mobile coverage is limited.

items.title: Man who sent threatening letters was 'drinking himself to sleep'
items.description: A man who sent threatening letters to a Sydney mosque was "drinking himself to sleep" and "fell into some type of internet rabbit hole", a court hears.
